question: Should I open a 9-hole or 18-hole mini-golf course in a tourist town, and what's the throughput math?
answer:
## Quick Take For a tourist town, **18 holes** wins if you can hit **40+ rounds/day**. At **9 holes**, you hit capacity faster but cap revenue. The real play: design for 4–6 minute holes and stagger starts. ## The Math (Owner-Operator Numbers) Start here—throughput is your ceiling: | Metric | 9-Hole | 18-Hole | |--------|--------|---------| | Par play time | 25–30 min | 50–60 min | | Capacity (12h open) | 24–28 rounds | 12–14 rounds | | Rounds @ 80% fill | **19–22** | **10–11** | | $18/round revenue | $342–396 | $180–198 | | High season boost | +40% = $480–555 | +40% = $252–277 | Tourist towns see **spiky demand**—lunch rush, evening clusters, weekend crushes. A **9-hole** course fills fast and turns people away at peak. An **18-hole** soaks that demand into the same slot without hitting a wall. Harris Miniature Golf and Putt-Putt Fun Center both proved **9-hole fits niche positioning** (wedge between arcade and real golf). Topgolf and Drive Shack went **18-hole+ with food/bars** to absorb higher throughput **AND** extend dwell time (profitability multiplier). ## Real Constraint: Bottleneck Flow Your per-hole par matters more than hole count: - **5-min holes** @ 18 = 3–4 rounds/hour max - **4-min holes** @ 18 = 4.5–5 rounds/hour - **Cost of Wisconsin** courses average **4.2 min/hole** on compact designs **Decision rule:** 1. **If you site in **high foot traffic** (boardwalk, downtown):** go **18-hole**—tourism density justifies the land/build cost; you'll fill it weekends. 2. **If you site **off-peak** (secondary strip, indoor mall):** go **9-hole**—lower overhead, faster ROI, still captures the niche. 3. **Test with pop-up:** rent a lot for **6 weeks**, run mock 9-hole. Track daily rounds. If you hit 80%+ capacity 3+ days/week, upgrade to **18-hole planning**. ## Revenue per Slot (Advanced) Account for **party size**: tourist rounds average **3.5–4 people**. A **9-hole** party ties up the course **25 min**. An **18-hole** party ties it up **55 min** but your per-person revenue is identical. The edge: 18-hole lets you **schedule** better, **upsell drinks/snacks** during play, and **hold evening leagues**. Topgolf's financial model flips this—they monetize **stay duration** with food & drink. Adventure Golf & Sports added **arcade** to justify the real estate.
